quality_gate.audit_note: rl_agent._passes_quality_gate() checks episodes + win_rate but NOT avg_reward. A model with avg_reward=-9140 (massive consistent losses) PASSES the gate as long as win_rate>=0.01 and episodes>=5. This is a SAFETY BUG — a catastrophically bad model can be loaded as 'trusted'.

rl_training_status.explanation: ml/train_rl.py's CLI takes a single --pair arg and trains ONE pair per invocation. There is NO loop over config.SYMBOLS, NO progress.json / completed_pairs file, and NO --resume flag. If interrupted midway through a 48-pair batch, the next run has no way to know which pairs were already done — it would either start from pair 0 again or rely on the operator to pass the right --pair arg. This is a critical missing feature.
rl_training_status.explanation_per_pair: train_rl.py saves to a SINGLE hardcoded path ml/rl_policy/ppo_forex_latest.zip regardless of --pair. Training GBPUSD then EURUSD OVERWRITES the same file. The meta JSON records the pair trained on, but the model file itself has no per-pair naming. There is NO way to have 48 separate RL policies loaded simultaneously.
rl_training_status.explanation_progress: RLPolicyStore (_registry.json) tracks versions v1/v2/v3... but each version is a SNAPSHOT of whatever pair was last trained. There is no field for 'which pairs have been trained' — only 'what is the latest version'. A resume from interrupted 48-pair training is impossible.
rl_training_status.explanation_corruption: RLPolicyStore.load_policy() only checks if the file exists at line 108-109 — it does NOT validate the .zip integrity, does NOT verify the model can be deserialized, and does NOT compare the meta's pair field to the requested pair. A truncated/corrupt .zip would silently fail at PPO.load() time inside rl_agent.load_model(), which is wrapped in try/except and falls back to heuristic mode — hiding the corruption from the operator.
rl_training_status.explanation_failure_logging: train_rl_agent() returns {'error': ...} on data-load failure and logs stage errors at ERROR level. But the CLI exit code is always 0 (no sys.exit(non-zero) on training error), so a CI/cron wrapper cannot detect failure from exit code alone.

findings.evidence: ml/rl_agent.py load_model() calls PPO.load(model_path) on the singleton init

stable_baselines3 is NOT installed in this env — RLAgent._check_sb3() returns False, load_model() returns False immediately, and predict() falls back to the heuristic path (source='heuristic'). The 'loaded' RL model has ZERO effect on trading decisions. Check that the production env has stable_baselines3 + torch installed.

findings.check: RL model pair matches backtest pair
findings.evidence: The single existing PPO model was trained on GBPUSD H1, but ml/rl_agent.get_rl_agent() is a SINGLETON with NO pair-awareness. When backtesting EURUSD H1, this GBPUSD-H1 model is loaded and its predict() output is fed into DecisionAgent's weighted vote as the 'rl_agent' signal. This is a SILENT PAIR MISMATCH — the model has never seen EURUSD H1 features during training, so its predictions are essentially noise dressed up as RL wisdom. Either train per-pair models (with per-pair filenames) or skip RL load entirely when the current pair != trained_on pair.

findings.check: ModelPredictor falls back to data/trained_models/ when memory/ml_models empty
findings.evidence: ModelPredictor._load_models() first checks memory/ml_models/{PAIR}_{TF}/ (empty in this repo — that dir is gitignored). If empty AND caller passes df_recent, falls back to _predict_institutional() which globs data/trained_models/{PAIR}/*/production/metadata.json. WARNING: AnalysisAgent passes df_recent (verified in source) so the fallback IS active — but only for pairs that have a 'production/' subdir, which is NOT how train_historical.py saves them (it saves directly to {PAIR}/{model_type}/, no production/ subdir). The institutional fallback therefore NEVER finds a model and ML ensemble returns NOT_READY — silently degrading to rule-based logic.

model_predictor._predict_institutional() looks for data/trained_models/{PAIR}/*/production/metadata.json. EURUSD/xgboost/production/ exists: False. If False, the institutional fallback will NOT find the model even though it exists at data/trained_models/EURUSD/xgboost/model.pkl.

checks.requirement: Train RL iterates over all 48 pairs
checks.evidence: ml/train_rl.py CLI takes --pair (single) arg. There is NO loop over config.SYMBOLS. To train 48 pairs the operator must invoke train_rl.py 48 times manually, with no tracking of which were done.

checks.requirement: ML retraining iterates over all 48 pairs
checks.evidence: ai/automated_retraining._retrain_models() loops over self.config.FOREX_PAIRS (which == config.SYMBOLS, 48 pairs).
ai/automated_retraining.py has NO progress.json, NO completed_pairs set, NO --resume flag. If interrupted midway, the next run starts from pair 0 again — retraining already-trained pairs.
Neither ml/train_rl.py nor ai/automated_retraining.py prints 'Training pairs: N/48' progress. The operator has no way to see at-a-glance how far through the 48-pair batch the training is.
